__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus datasource scraping the Janus /metrics endpoint.

description: Janus secrets manager — seal state, HTTP traffic and latency, scheduler liveness, engine failures, DB pool, audit chain, and Go runtime. Every panel is backed by a metric the server actually exports on /metrics.

panels.description:
A sealed Janus holds no master key in memory and returns 503 for every secret operation. This is the single most important signal on the board.

`janus_sealed` (gauge): 1 = sealed, 0 = unsealed.
panels.title: Seal state

panels.description: Prometheus' synthetic `up` series for the Janus target. 0 = the scrape failed (process down, wrong metrics token, or network partition).
panels.title: Scrape up

panels.description: Process age, from `janus_start_time_seconds` (gauge, unix seconds). A repeatedly resetting uptime means the container is crash-looping.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: `janus_build_info` (gauge, always 1) carries the running version and commit as labels.
panels.title: Build

panels.description: `janus_http_requests_total` is a counter labelled method/route/status; `status` is the full numeric code (not a class). Stacked so total throughput and its composition read at a glance.
panels.title: Request rate by status

panels.description: Quantiles interpolated from the `janus_http_request_duration_seconds` histogram (buckets: 5ms … 10s). The top bucket is 10s, so values above it read as ~10s.
panels.title: Request latency quantiles

panels.description: Top 10 chi route *patterns* (e.g. `/v1/projects/{pid}/configs`) — never concrete paths, so no project ids or secret keys appear here. Unmatched paths collapse to `route="unmatched"`.
panels.title: Request rate by route

panels.description: Server-fault ratio. Note that 503 is also how a **sealed** server answers secret operations, so a spike here right after a restart usually means 'not unsealed yet', not 'broken'. Cross-check the seal panel.
panels.title: 5xx error ratio

panels.description: Unauthenticated (401) and RBAC-denied (403) request rate. A sustained climb on a secrets manager is worth a look — credential stuffing, an expired service token, or a misscoped token in CI. Correlate with the audit log's denied-only export.
panels.title: Auth denials (401 / 403)

panels.description: Slowest 10 route patterns at p95. The duration histogram is labelled method/route only (no status), so this mixes successes and failures.
panels.title: p95 latency by route
Schedulers & engines — is background work still running?

panels.description: Seconds since each engine loop last ticked, from `janus_scheduler_last_tick_seconds` (gauge, unix seconds, labelled `engine`). Engines: `rotation`, `sync`, `dynamic` (all 60s by default), plus `sync_verify` and `backup` when enabled. A stalled scheduler means rotations, syncs and lease revocation silently stop — nothing errors, work just never happens. A series only appears after its first tick, so a disabled engine is absent rather than stale.
panels.title: Scheduler tick age by engine

panels.description: Recorded run rows with status=failure. Both are **gauges** (a scrape-time COUNT over the run-history tables), not counters — so use a delta against an offset, never `rate()`/`increase()`, when alerting.
panels.title: Failed rotation / sync runs

panels.description: Live dynamic Postgres credentials (`janus_dynamic_leases_active`, gauge). A ramp that never comes down suggests leases are being issued but not revoked/expired — check the `dynamic` scheduler tick age panel.
panels.title: Active dynamic leases

panels.description: pgx pool gauge, `state` ∈ total / idle / acquired / max. `acquired` pinned at `max` means requests are queueing on connection checkout.
panels.title: DB pool connections by state

panels.description: acquired ÷ max. Sustained >80% means the pool is the bottleneck — raise `JANUS_DB_MAX_CONNS` or find the slow query.
panels.title: DB pool saturation

panels.description: `janus_audit_head_seq` (gauge) is the sequence number of the hash-chain head. It only ever moves up. A flat head while requests are still flowing means audited mutations have stopped — every audited write fails closed, so that is an outage, not quiet. `deriv()` (not `rate()`) is the gauge-correct slope. Chain *verification* is O(events) and deliberately not scraped — use `GET /v1/audit/verify`.
panels.title: Audit chain head

panels.description: `janus_go_goroutines` (gauge). A monotonic climb across hours is the classic goroutine-leak shape.
panels.title: Goroutines

panels.description: `janus_go_heap_alloc_bytes` (gauge) — live heap objects. Compare against the container memory limit.
panels.title: Heap in use

panels.description: Fraction of wall time spent in GC stop-the-world pauses. The underlying series is *typed* gauge but is cumulative and monotonic within a process, so `rate()` is safe and additionally handles the reset on restart.
panels.title: GC pause rate
